timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Why are you so concerned about student STEM learning opportunities?
What is it that makes you want to dedicate so much of your time and energy and resources
into making more STEM learning opportunities available to all students?
I think it's fundamental to the health and welfare of California and United States.
The most countries, but my interest is California and United States.
And I think that is the foundation from which prosperity and public welfare is built.
And that coupling science and math and technology,
engineering to ingenuity, which goes with it,
is what is given America, its position in the world, is the world leader in economics.
So if you walk into a California classroom and STEM is working,
what are you going to see in that classroom?
I think you would see that the kids are interested, enthusiastic, and I learn it.
And I think you would see them dealing with real world problems
in some sort of experimental way,
that really keeps them involved and interested in feeling that it's interesting and worthwhile.
Those of us involved with CSI net believe that STEM is for all children.
Your views?
I think it certainly is, it's for all people really,
where you really get it is in school,
and where you ought to be getting it, it's starting right in the first grade, or preschool.
But you get interested in dealing with things and what makes wheels go around and what wheels are,
which is all part of STEM.
And whether you want to go into science or engineering, or be a mathematician, or other sciences,
I think the STEM Education Foundation is something that builds toward, I think,
an outstanding professional life.
For California to achieve economic vitality, what would an innovative workforce look like?
And how does STEM education play a role?
I think an innovative workforce is built on knowledge of science, math, engineering,
and that type of thing, and it's just a foundation to it.
I think we're just running behind here in California.
The public schools generally have fallen from one of the best in the country,
to one of the worst in the country.
Well, most of the tests and information that I have seen, and I think it's just a bad situation
where we are, and I think we've got to find a way to give more attention,
and get the school systems turned around where they do the right kind of job,
but getting the kids enthused and inspired and learning.
